chunks: Ibn Qulawayh from Ja'far ibn Muhammad from 'Abdullah ibn Nahik from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from 'Ali from Jamil from some of our companions from one of the Imams (peace be upon them) that he said:
"A man is compelled only to provide for the maintenance of his parents and his children."

I said to Jamil, 'And what about the wife?' He said, 'Our companions have narrated from one of the Imams (peace be upon them) that if he clothes her with what covers her private parts and feeds her with what sustains her strength, she remains with him, otherwise he divorces her.'
He said, I said to Jamil, 'Is he compelled to provide for his sister?' He said, 'If he were compelled to provide for his sister, that would be contrary to the narration.'
ai.seo_question: What are the compulsory financial maintenance obligations of a husband in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from the *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the scope of compulsory financial maintenance (nafaqah) in Shia jurisprudence, distinguishing between mandatory support for parents and children and the conditional nature of spousal support, which requires the wife to remain with her husband in exchange for adequate sustenance and clothing. The text further establishes that while supporting siblings is permissible, it is not legally compelled (mujbar) unless specified by other evidence, highlighting the precision of juristic deduction in family law. This ruling is foundational for understanding the economic rights and duties within the Shia family structure as derived from the Imams.
